Anthony Scaramucci joins Vlad to break down Warren Buffett’s harsh criticism of Bitcoin, including “rat poison squared,” and why the SkyBridge Capital founder believes some legendary investors simply haven’t done the homework. Scaramucci compares Buffett’s stance with major financial figures who changed their minds, including Ray Dalio, Larry Fink, Stan Druckenmiller and JP Morgan Wealth Management, while discussing Bitcoin ETFs, Ethereum, Solana and the future of crypto adoption.

The conversation also turns to meme coins, including Donald Trump’s coin, his wife’s coin and Hunter Biden-related crypto projects, with Scaramucci calling them harmful “gambling tokens” for the industry. He also discusses his book, *All the Wrong Moves*, examining China’s WTO entry, the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, the bank bailouts, Occupy Wall Street, the Tea Party and the rise of MAGA. A wide-ranging discussion on money, politics, gratitude and America’s economic future.

recentItems.title: Lil Jungle Boy on Being a Drug Runner at 7, Joining the Bloods at 10 (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
In this VladTV interview, Lil Jungle Boy details his turbulent childhood from South Central Los Angeles to foster care in Louisiana and Chicago. Born at Martin Luther King Hospital in L.A., he says his mother’s drug addiction led to him being placed in the system, while questions around his biological father left him disconnected from family early on. He recalls being exposed to the streets as a child in New Orleans, where he says adults used young kids as runners during the crack era. The conversation also touches on Freeway Ricky Ross and Wack100’s debate over so-called “crack babies.” Lil Jungle Boy later returned to Los Angeles, reconnected with relatives, and moved into the Jungles, a Blood neighborhood, where he says he was put on around age 10 or 11 despite his stepfather’s objections. A raw look at foster care, gang culture, survival, and South Central history.

--------
In this VladTV interview, former Medellín Cartel co-founder Carlos Lehder reflects on freedom after 33 years in U.S. prison and explains how a life that once generated vast drug money ended with no property, no fortune, and book sales as his only income. Lehder discusses returning to Colombia after time in Germany, life in Medellín today, and his book *Vida y muerte del cartel de Medellín*, now translated into English.

He also addresses Boston George (George Jung), Pablo Escobar’s legacy, El Chapo’s life-plus-30-year sentence in U.S. federal court, extradition, Florence, Colorado, and why he believes the narco era is collapsing under modern law enforcement technology. From the Ukraine-Russia war to Colombia’s new political direction, Lehder offers a rare firsthand perspective on crime, punishment, and the cost of chasing power through drug trafficking.

--------
William Noguera sits down with Vlad to reflect on spending 42 years in prison and the hard lessons learned from life on death row. Now 62, Noguera explains why he would tell his 18-year-old self to “walk away,” discusses the violent “convict code” inside level four prison yards, and describes how reputation, respect, and survival shape prison society. He also addresses questions about the Mexican Mafia, rehabilitation, remorse, and taking responsibility before the parole board.

Noguera opens up about the murder that changed his life, his regret for the victim, and how he worked to rebuild his humanity behind bars. He also discusses helping solve four cold case homicides tied to a serial killer, a story featured in Peacock’s Death Row Confidential: Secrets of a Serial Killer and his book Through the Lens of a Monster.
